artists.negativeHint: exoticizing fantasy costume kitsch
artists.bio: Pierre Edouard Leopold Verger, alias Fatumbi or Fátúmbí was a photographer, self-taught ethnographer, and babalawo who devoted most of his life to the study of the African diaspora — the slave trade, the African-based religions of the new world, and the resulting cultural and economical flows from and to Africa.

artists.name: Katy Grannan-adjacent roadside portrait
artists.styleLock: Photoreal bright daylight roadside portraiture: direct gaze, ordinary American edges, unvarnished honesty, hard noon light.
artists.negativeHint: soft Rembrandt studio only, fantasy makeup
artists.bio: Katy Grannan is an American photographer and filmmaker. She made the feature-length film, The Nine. Her work is held in the collections of the Metropolitan Museum of Art, Museum of Modern Art, Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, and Whitney Museum of American Art.

artists.name: Rembrandt
artists.styleLock: Oil painting in the spirit of Rembrandt: warm chiaroscuro, thick luminous flesh tones against deep umber ground, quiet psychological gravity, visible brush and glaze depth.
artists.negativeHint: flat digital shading, neon colors, anime eyes
artists.bio: Rembrandt Harmenszoon van Rijn, known mononymously as Rembrandt, was a Dutch Golden Age painter, printmaker, and draughtsman. He is generally considered one of the greatest visual artists in the history of Western art. It is estimated that Rembrandt's surviving works amount to about three hundred paintings, three hundred etchings, and several hundred drawings.

artists.name: Johannes Vermeer
artists.styleLock: Oil painting in the spirit of Vermeer: cool north-window light, pearl highlights, intimate interior geometry, serene stillness, finely observed fabrics and maps.
artists.negativeHint: harsh spotlight, cluttered baroque drama, modern gadgets
artists.bio: Johannes Vermeer was a Dutch painter who specialized in domestic interior scenes of middle-class life. He is considered one of the greatest painters of the Dutch Golden Age. During his lifetime, he was a moderately successful provincial genre painter, recognized in Delft and The Hague. He produced relatively few paintings, primarily earning his living as an art dealer. He was not wealthy; at his death, his wife was left in debt.

artists.name: Claude Monet
artists.styleLock: Impressionist oil painting in the spirit of Monet: broken color, shimmering light on water and air, soft edges, vibrating complementary hues, outdoor atmosphere over hard line.
artists.negativeHint: hard outlines, photographic sharpness, muddy brown soup
artists.bio: Oscar-Claude Monet was a French painter and founder of Impressionism who is seen as a key precursor to modernism, especially in his attempts to paint nature as he perceived it. During his long career, he was the most consistent and prolific practitioner of Impressionism's philosophy of expressing one's perceptions of nature, especially as applied to plein air (outdoor) landscape painting. The term "Impressionism" is derived from the title of his painting Impression, Sunrise, which was exhibited in 1874 at the First Impressionist Exhibition, initiated by Monet and a number of like-minded artists as an alternative to the Salon.

artists.name: Vincent van Gogh
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Van Gogh: energetic impasto swirls, emotional color, rhythmic directional strokes, thick paint ridges catching light, intense sky and field energy.
artists.negativeHint: smooth airbrush, photoreal skin pores, flat vector shapes
artists.bio: Vincent Willem van Gogh was a Dutch Post-Impressionist painter who is among the most famous and influential figures in the history of Western art. In just over a decade he created about 2,100 artworks, including around 860 oil paintings, most of them in the last two years of his life. They include landscapes, still lifes, portraits and self-portraits, and are characterised by bold colours and dramatic, impulsive and expressive brushwork that contributed to the foundations of modern art. His suicide at age 37 followed years of mental illness and poverty.

artists.name: Katsushika Hokusai
artists.styleLock: Ukiyo-e woodblock print spirit of Hokusai: bold contour, flat layered color, stylized wave and mountain rhythm, decorative pattern, Japanese printmaking clarity.
artists.negativeHint: western oil impasto, photoreal foam, 3D CGI
artists.bio: Katsushika Hokusai  was a Japanese ukiyo-e artist of the Edo period, active as a painter and printmaker. His woodblock print series Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji includes the iconic print The Great Wave off Kanagawa. Hokusai was instrumental in developing ukiyo-e from a style of portraiture largely focused on courtesans and actors into a much broader style of art that focused on landscapes, plants, and animals. His works had a significant influence on Vincent van Gogh and Claude Monet during the wave of Japonisme that spread across Europe in the late 19th century.

artists.name: Alphonse Mucha
artists.styleLock: Art Nouveau illustration in the spirit of Mucha: elegant flowing hair and floral halos, pastel decorative panels, graceful line, ornamental framing motifs without readable text.
artists.negativeHint: brutalist geometry, photoreal pores, heavy metal dark tones
artists.bio: Alfons Maria Mucha, known in English as Alphonse Mucha, was a Czech painter, illustrator, and graphic artist. Living in Paris during the Art Nouveau period, he was widely known for his distinctly stylised and decorative theatrical posters, particularly those of Sarah Bernhardt. He produced illustrations, advertisements, decorative panels, as well as designs, which became among the best-known images of the period.

artists.name: Edward Hopper
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Edward Hopper: lonely architectural light, long shadows, quiet American stillness, clear planes of color, cinematic solitude.
artists.negativeHint: busy crowds, neon cyberpunk, impressionist blur
artists.bio: Edward Hopper was an American realist painter and printmaker. He is one of America's most renowned artists and known for his skill in depicting modern American life and landscapes.

artists.name: Georgia O'Keeffe
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Georgia O'Keeffe: magnified organic forms, smooth sculptural petals and bones, desert pastel palette, monumental close-up simplicity.
artists.negativeHint: busy collage, tiny scattered details, harsh comic outlines
artists.bio: Georgia Totto O'Keeffe was an American modernist painter and draftswoman whose career spanned seven decades and whose work remained largely independent of major art movements. Called the "Mother of American modernism", O'Keeffe gained international recognition for her paintings of natural forms, particularly flowers, hills and desert-inspired landscapes, which were often drawn from and related to places and environments in which she lived. Although she was a figure associated with interpretations regarding feminism, she did not want to be seen as a "woman artist", she wanted to be seen as an artist.

artists.name: Sidney Nolan
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Sidney Nolan: Australian mythic landscape, bold simplified forms, enamel-like color planes, harsh sun, Ned Kelly-era atmosphere without copying protected icons literally.
artists.negativeHint: European cottage pastoral, soft watercolor haze only
artists.bio: Sir Sidney Robert Nolan was one of the leading Australian artists of the 20th century. Working in a wide variety of media, his oeuvre is among the most diverse and prolific in all of modern art. He is best known for his series of paintings on legends from Australian history, most famously that of Ned Kelly, the bushranger and outlaw. Nolan's stylised depiction of Kelly's armour has become an icon of Australian art.

artists.name: Brett Whiteley
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Brett Whiteley: sensual calligraphic line, Sydney harbour light, erotic curve and bird motif energy, vivid ultramarine and warm flesh accents, restless modern lyricism.
artists.negativeHint: stiff academic realism, dull grey palette
artists.bio: Brett Whiteley was an Australian artist. He is represented in the collections of all the large Australian galleries, and was twice winner of the Archibald, Wynne and Sulman prizes. He held many exhibitions, and lived and painted in Australia as well as Italy, the United Kingdom, Fiji and the United States.

artists.name: Margaret Preston
artists.styleLock: Modernist still-life and flora in the spirit of Margaret Preston: strong design, flattened decorative native plants, bold color blocks, print-aware composition, Australian domestic modernism.
artists.negativeHint: Victorian clutter, photoreal dewdrop macro only
artists.bio: Margaret Rose Preston was an Australian painter, printmaker and writer on art who is regarded as one of Australia's leading modernists of the early 20th century. In her quest to foster an Australian "national art", she was also one of the first non-Indigenous Australian artists to use Aboriginal motifs in her work. Her works are distinctively signed MP.

artists.name: J.M.W. Turner
artists.styleLock: Romantic oil painting in the spirit of Turner: luminous vaporous light, dissolving forms in mist and spray, golden and storm-grey atmosphere, sublime weather drama.
artists.negativeHint: hard comic outlines, flat poster color, crisp product photography
artists.bio: Joseph Mallord William Turner, known in his time as William Turner, was an English Romantic painter and elevated the status of landscape painting. Turner is regarded as one of the greatest and most influential British painters, as well as a precursor to Impressionism.

artists.name: Caravaggio
artists.styleLock: Baroque oil painting in the spirit of Caravaggio: extreme tenebrism, single harsh light carving figures from darkness, raw realism, dramatic gesture, earth pigments.
artists.negativeHint: pastel impressionism, cute cartoon faces, even softbox light
artists.bio: Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio, known mononymously as Caravaggio, was an Italian painter active in Rome for a significant portion of his artistic life. He began his apprenticeship in Milan in 1584, and during the final four years of his life, he moved between Naples, Malta, and Sicily. His paintings have been characterized by art critics as combining a realistic observation of the human state, both physical and emotional, with a dramatic use of lighting, which had a formative influence on Baroque painting.

artists.name: Gustav Klimt
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Klimt: ornamental gold patterning, mosaic-like surfaces, intimate figures wrapped in decorative geometry, jewel tones against flattened space.
artists.negativeHint: plain photoreal office scenes, rough charcoal only
artists.bio: Gustav Klimt was an Austrian symbolist painter and a founding member of the Vienna Secession movement. His work helped define the Art Nouveau style in Europe. Klimt is known for his paintings, murals, sketches, and other objets d'art. Klimt's primary subject was the female body, and his works are marked by a frank eroticism. Amongst his figurative works, which include allegories and portraits, he painted landscapes. He is best known for The Kiss and Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I. Among the artists of the Vienna Secession, Klimt was the most influenced by Japanese art and its methods.

artists.name: Henri Matisse
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Matisse: joyous Fauvist color, simplified contour, decorative interior pattern, flat yet lively planes, Mediterranean warmth.
artists.negativeHint: brown academic underpainting only, photoreal skin detail
artists.bio: Henri Émile Benoît Matisse was a French visual artist, known for both his use of colour and his fluid and original draughtsmanship. He was a draughtsman, printmaker, and sculptor, but is known primarily as a painter.

artists.name: Paul Cézanne
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Cézanne: constructive brush planes, solid fruit and mountain volumes, cool-warm modulation, deliberate unfinished edges, structural seeing.
artists.negativeHint: slick airbrush gradients, anime lineart
artists.bio: Paul Cézanne (Post-Impressionism FR). Painting in the spirit of Cézanne: constructive brush planes, solid fruit and mountain volumes, cool-warm modulation, deliberate unfinished edges, structural seeing. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: structure, still-life, europe.

artists.name: David Hockney
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of David Hockney: clear acrylic color, swimming-pool blues, crisp shadows, cheerful modern domestic geometry, bright California/Australian outdoor light feel.
artists.negativeHint: muddy tonalism, gothic darkness, heavy impasto brown
artists.bio: David Hockney was a British painter, stage designer and photographer. As an important contributor to the pop art movement of the 1960s, he is considered one of the most influential British artists of the 20th and 21st centuries. He was known for his vivid, stylised realism and championed figurative work, often in a bold style, during a period when abstract art predominated.

artists.name: Frida Kahlo-adjacent symbolism
artists.styleLock: Symbolic personal painting: frontal intimate portrait energy, vivid folk color, surreal personal emblems, botanical and animal companions, clear narrative detail without text.
artists.negativeHint: generic stock selfie, bland corporate portrait
artists.bio: Magdalena Carmen Frida Kahlo y Calderón was a Mexican painter known for her many portraits, self-portraits, and works inspired by the nature and artifacts of Mexico. Inspired by the country's popular culture, she employed a naïve folk art style to explore questions of identity, postcolonialism, gender, class, and race in Mexican society. Her paintings often had strong autobiographical elements and mixed realism with fantasy. In addition to belonging to the post-revolutionary Mexicayotl movement, which sought to define a Mexican identity, Kahlo has been described as a surrealist or magical realist. She is also known for painting about her experience of chronic pain. Her 1940 self-portrait tit...

artists.name: René Magritte
artists.styleLock: Surreal painting in the spirit of Magritte: clean illusionistic rendering, quiet sky and bowler-hat absurdity of displaced objects, deadpan lighting, philosophical visual pun without captions.
artists.negativeHint: messy expressionist smear, horror gore
artists.bio: René Magritte (Surrealism BE). Surreal painting in the spirit of Magritte: clean illusionistic rendering, quiet sky and bowler-hat absurdity of displaced objects, deadpan lighting, philosophical visual pun without captions. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: surrealism, europe.

artists.name: Salvador Dalí
artists.styleLock: Surreal oil painting in the spirit of Dalí: hyper-crisp desert light, melting metamorphosis, long shadows, meticulous miniature detail in vast empty plains.
artists.negativeHint: soft impressionist blur, cute kawaii forms
artists.bio: Salvador Dalí (Surrealism ES). Surreal oil painting in the spirit of Dalí: hyper-crisp desert light, melting metamorphosis, long shadows, meticulous miniature detail in vast empty plains. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: surrealism, europe.

artists.name: James McNeill Whistler
artists.styleLock: Tonalist painting in the spirit of Whistler: soft nocturne greys and blues, musical arrangement of muted tones, foggy harbors, restrained elegance.
artists.negativeHint: high-chroma neon, hard comic outlines
artists.bio: James Abbott McNeill Whistler was an American painter in oils and watercolor, and printmaker, based primarily in the United Kingdom. He eschewed sentimentality and moral allusion in painting and was a leading proponent of the credo "art for art's sake".

artists.name: John Singer Sargent
artists.styleLock: Oil portraiture in the spirit of Sargent: bravura brushwork, luminous fabrics, confident unfinished edges, aristocratic light, lively likeness without photographic hardness.
artists.negativeHint: stiff mannequin pose, plastic skin, AI melted hands emphasis
artists.bio: John Singer Sargent was an American expatriate artist, considered the "leading portrait painter of his generation" for his evocations of Belle Époque and Edwardian-era luxury. He created roughly 900 oil paintings and more than 2,000 watercolors, as well as countless sketches and charcoal drawings. His oeuvre documents worldwide travel, from Venice to the Tyrol, Corfu, Capri, Spain, the Middle East, Montana, Maine, and Florida.

artists.name: John William Waterhouse
artists.styleLock: Pre-Raphaelite narrative painting spirit: rich jewel colors, mythic storytelling, detailed flora, luminous skin, romantic atmosphere.
artists.negativeHint: modern streetwear, cyberpunk city
artists.bio: John William Waterhouse was an English painter known for working first in the Academic style and for then embracing the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood's style and subject matter. His paintings are known for their depictions of women from ancient Greek mythology, Arthurian legend, and the works of William Shakespeare. A high proportion depict a single young and beautiful woman in a historical costume and setting, though there are some ventures into Orientalist painting and genre painting, still mostly featuring women.

artists.name: Mark Rothko-adjacent color field
artists.styleLock: Abstract color-field painting: soft-edged luminous rectangles of color hovering in atmospheric wash, meditative emotion, no figurative detail, gallery-scale presence.
artists.negativeHint: hard geometric Bauhaus only, busy figurative scenes
artists.bio: Mark Rothko was a Latvian-born American abstract painter. He is best known for his color field paintings that depicted irregular and painterly rectangular regions of color, which he produced from 1949 to 1970. Although Rothko did not personally subscribe to any one school, he is associated with the American abstract expressionism movement of modern art.

artists.name: Jackson Pollock-adjacent action
artists.styleLock: Abstract expressionist action painting: layered drips and spatters, all-over energy, tangled rhythmic lines, industrial paint density, no central figure.
artists.negativeHint: neat illustration characters, clean vector logos
artists.bio: Paul Jackson Pollock was an American painter. A major figure in the abstract expressionist movement, he was widely noticed for his "drip technique" of pouring or splashing liquid household paint onto a horizontal surface, enabling him to view and paint his canvases from all angles. It was called all-over painting and action painting, because Pollock covered the entire canvas and used the force of his whole body to paint, often in a frenetic dancing style. This extreme form of abstraction divided critics: some praised the immediacy of the creation, while others derided the random effects.

artists.name: Andrew Wyeth
artists.styleLock: Tempera-like realist painting in the spirit of Wyeth: dry grass textures, austere rural light, quiet melancholy, precise observation, muted earth palette.
artists.negativeHint: tropical paradise colors, cartoon exaggeration
artists.bio: Andrew Newell Wyeth was an American visual artist and one of the best-known American artists of the middle 20th century. Though he considered himself to be an "abstractionist", Wyeth was primarily a realist painter who worked in a regionalist style, often painting the land and people of his hometown in Chadds Ford, Pennsylvania, and his summer home in Cushing, Maine.

artists.name: Jean-Michel Basquiat-adjacent neo-expressionism
artists.styleLock: Neo-expressionist painting energy: raw scrawl, crown-like motifs, layered textural marks without readable words, urgent color, street-poetry intensity.
artists.negativeHint: clean corporate illustration, photoreal portraits only
artists.bio: Jean-Michel Basquiat was an American artist who rose to success during the 1980s as part of the Neo-expressionism movement.

artists.name: Sumi-e ink painting
artists.styleLock: Sumi-e ink painting: expressive black brush on warm paper, controlled voids, misty mountains or bamboo economy of stroke, contemplative asymmetry.
artists.negativeHint: heavy western oil impasto, full-color photoreal
artists.bio: Sumi-e ink painting (classical JP). Sumi-e ink painting: expressive black brush on warm paper, controlled voids, misty mountains or bamboo economy of stroke, contemplative asymmetry. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: ink, east-asian, asia, japan.

artists.name: Heidelberg School
artists.styleLock: Australian Heidelberg School plein-air painting: dappled eucalyptus shade, golden paddocks, blue distant ranges, informal bush light, colonial-era picnic atmosphere without text.
artists.negativeHint: European thatched cottages as default, neon skies
artists.bio: Heidelberg School (1890s AU). Australian Heidelberg School plein-air painting: dappled eucalyptus shade, golden paddocks, blue distant ranges, informal bush light, colonial-era picnic atmosphere without text. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: australian, impressionism, oceania.

artists.name: Russell Drysdale
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Russell Drysdale: elongated outback figures, sparse red earth towns, harsh noon light, psychological distance, dry Australian interior.
artists.negativeHint: lush rainforest default, cute cartoon townsfolk
artists.bio: Sir George Russell Drysdale, also known as Tass Drysdale, was an Australian artist. He won the prestigious Wynne Prize for Sofala in 1947, and represented Australia at the Venice Biennale in 1954. He was influenced by abstract and surrealist art, and "created a new vision of the Australian scene as revolutionary and influential as that of Tom Roberts".

artists.name: Arthur Boyd
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Arthur Boyd: mythic Australian landscape with expressive figures, warm earth and fiery sky, moral allegory energy, rich oil textures.
artists.negativeHint: cold Scandinavian minimalism, stock photo realism
artists.bio: Arthur Merric Bloomfield Boyd was a leading Australian painter of the middle to late 20th century. Boyd's work ranges from impressionist renderings of Australian landscape to starkly expressionist figuration, and many canvases feature both. Several famous works set Biblical stories against the Australian landscape, such as The Expulsion (1947–48), now at the Art Gallery of New South Wales. Having a strong social conscience, Boyd's work deals with humanitarian issues and universal themes of love, loss and shame.

artists.name: Caspar David Friedrich
artists.styleLock: Romantic landscape painting in the spirit of Friedrich: lone Rückenfigur scale, misty cliffs and ruins, sublime dawn or dusk, contemplative silence.
artists.negativeHint: busy tourist selfie energy, pop-art dots
artists.bio: Caspar David Friedrich was a German Romantic landscape painter, generally considered the most important German artist of his generation, whose often symbolic, and anti-classical work, conveys a subjective, emotional response to the natural world. Friedrich's paintings often set contemplative human figures silhouetted against night skies, morning mists, barren trees or Gothic ruins. Art historian Christopher John Murray described their presence, in diminished perspective, amid expansive landscapes, as reducing the figures to a scale that directs "the viewer's gaze towards their metaphysical dimension".

artists.name: Hieronymus Bosch-adjacent fantasy
artists.styleLock: Northern Renaissance fantasy panel energy: dense allegorical detail, strange hybrid creatures, panoramic moral landscape, jewel-like tempera clarity—imaginative, not grotesque gore.
artists.negativeHint: minimal modern poster, empty color field
artists.bio: Hieronymus Bosch was a Dutch painter from Brabant. He is one of the most notable representatives of the Early Netherlandish painting school. His work, generally oil on oak wood, mainly contains fantastic illustrations of religious concepts and narratives. Within his lifetime, his work was collected in the Netherlands, Austria, and Spain, and widely copied, especially his macabre and nightmarish depictions of hell.

artists.name: Marc Chagall
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Chagall: floating figures, village dream logic, lyrical blues and reds, folk-memory tenderness, airborne perspective.
artists.negativeHint: hard photoreal documentary only, brutalist grey
artists.bio: Marc Chagall was a Russian and French artist of Jewish ancestry. An early modernist, he was associated with the École de Paris, as well as several major artistic styles and created works in a wide range of artistic formats, including painting, drawings, book illustrations, stained glass, stage sets, ceramics, tapestries and fine art prints.

artists.name: Picasso Blue Period-adjacent
artists.styleLock: Early modernist painting: elongated melancholic figures, cool blue-green monochrome, simplified form, quiet empathy.
artists.negativeHint: cubist shatter overload, neon pop
artists.bio: Picasso Blue Period-adjacent (early 20th c. ES/FR). Early modernist painting: elongated melancholic figures, cool blue-green monochrome, simplified form, quiet empathy. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: modernism, europe.

artists.name: Picasso Cubism-adjacent
artists.styleLock: Analytical/synthetic Cubist painting energy: fractured planes, multiple viewpoints, ochre-grey or collage-like facets, still-life and figure reconstructed as geometry.
artists.negativeHint: smooth photorealism, single-point perspective only
artists.bio: Picasso Cubism-adjacent (early 20th c. ES/FR). Analytical/synthetic Cubist painting energy: fractured planes, multiple viewpoints, ochre-grey or collage-like facets, still-life and figure reconstructed as geometry. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: cubism, modernism, europe.

artists.name: Georges Braque
artists.styleLock: Cubist painting in the spirit of Braque: muted ochres and greys, overlapping faceted forms, textured papier-collé feel, quiet structural still-life.
artists.negativeHint: neon pop colors, soft watercolor blooms
artists.bio: Georges Braque was a major 20th-century French painter, collagist, draughtsman, printmaker and sculptor. His most notable contributions were in his alliance with Fauvism from 1905, and the role he played in the development of Cubism. Braque's work between 1908 and 1912 is closely associated with that of his colleague Pablo Picasso. Their respective Cubist works were indistinguishable for many years, yet the quiet nature of Braque was partially eclipsed by the fame and notoriety of Picasso.

artists.name: Piet Mondrian-adjacent neoplasticism
artists.styleLock: Neoplastic abstract graphic: orthogonal black grid, primary red yellow blue planes, white ground, perfect balance, no diagonals or curves.
artists.negativeHint: organic floral, photoreal scenes
artists.bio: Pieter Cornelis Mondriaan, known after 1911 as Piet Mondrian, was a Dutch painter and art theoretician, who is regarded as one of the greatest artists of the 20th century. He was one of the pioneers of 20th-century abstract art, as he changed his artistic direction from figurative painting to an increasingly abstract style, until he reached a point where his artistic vocabulary was taken down to simple geometric elements.

artists.name: M.C. Escher-adjacent tessellation
artists.styleLock: Graphic tessellation and impossible architecture: precise line, interlocking metamorphosis, cool intellectual puzzle space, lithograph clarity.
artists.negativeHint: loose watercolor bloom, soft portraiture
artists.bio:
Maurits Cornelis Escher was a Dutch graphic artist who made woodcuts, lithographs, and mezzotints, many of which were inspired by mathematics.
Despite wide popular interest, for most of his life Escher was neglected in the art world, even in his native Netherlands. He was 70 before a retrospective exhibition was held. In the late twentieth century, he became more widely appreciated, and in the twenty-first century he has been celebrated in exhibitions around the world.

artists.name: Michelangelo
artists.styleLock: High Renaissance painting/fresco spirit of Michelangelo: heroic anatomy, sculptural musculature, monumental figures, dynamic contraposto, classical grandeur.
artists.negativeHint: cute chibi proportions, flat poster color only
artists.bio: Michelangelo di Lodovico Buonarroti Simoni, known mononymously as Michelangelo, was an Italian sculptor, painter, architect, and poet of the High Renaissance. He was born in the Republic of Florence but was mostly active in Rome from his 30s onwards. His work was inspired by models from classical antiquity and had a lasting influence on Western art. Michelangelo's creative abilities and mastery in a range of artistic arenas define him as an archetypal Renaissance man, along with his rival and elder contemporary, Leonardo da Vinci. Given the sheer volume of surviving correspondence, sketches, and reminiscences, Michelangelo is one of the best-documented artists of the 16th century. He was lau...

artists.name: Leonardo da Vinci
artists.styleLock: Renaissance painting in the spirit of Leonardo: soft sfumato transitions, mysterious atmosphere, precise observation of nature, subtle psychological presence.
artists.negativeHint: hard comic outlines, neon cyberpunk
artists.bio: Leonardo di ser Piero da Vinci was an Italian polymath of the High Renaissance who was active as a painter, draughtsman, engineer, scientist, theorist, sculptor, and architect. While his fame initially rested on his achievements as a painter, he has also become known for his notebooks, in which he made drawings and notes on a variety of subjects, including anatomy, astronomy, botany, cartography, painting, and palaeontology. Leonardo is widely regarded as a genius who epitomised the Renaissance humanist ideal, and his collective works contributed to the development of European art to an extent rivalled only by that of his younger contemporary Michelangelo.

artists.name: Sandro Botticelli
artists.styleLock: Early Renaissance tempera spirit of Botticelli: graceful linear figures, mythic allegory, delicate florals, pale luminous skin, lyrical composition.
artists.negativeHint: heavy impasto expressionism, photoreal pores
artists.bio: Alessandro di Mariano di Vanni Filipepi, better known as Sandro Botticelli or simply Botticelli, was an Italian painter of the Early Renaissance. Botticelli's posthumous reputation suffered until the late 19th century, when he was rediscovered by the Pre-Raphaelites who stimulated a reappraisal of his work. Since then, his paintings have been seen to represent the linear grace of late Italian Gothic and some Early Renaissance painting, even though they date from the latter half of the Italian Renaissance period.

artists.name: Raphael
artists.styleLock: High Renaissance harmony in the spirit of Raphael: balanced composition, serene Madonnas and architecture, clear sweet color, idealized clarity.
artists.negativeHint: chaotic drip painting, horror surrealism
artists.bio: Raffaello Sanzio da Urbino, now generally known in English as Raphael, was an Italian painter and architect of the High Renaissance. His work is admired for its clarity of form, ease of composition, and visual achievement of the Neoplatonic ideal of human grandeur. Together with Leonardo da Vinci and Michelangelo, he forms the traditional trinity of great masters of that period.

artists.name: Titian
artists.styleLock: Venetian Renaissance oil in the spirit of Titian: rich colorito, glowing flesh, luxurious fabrics, atmospheric depth, sensual mythic narrative.
artists.negativeHint: flat graphic poster, cold minimal grey
artists.bio: Tiziano Vecellio, Latinized as Titianus, hence known in English as Titian, was an Italian Renaissance painter. The most important artist of Renaissance Venetian painting, he was born in Pieve di Cadore, near Belluno.

artists.name: Peter Paul Rubens
artists.styleLock: Flemish Baroque painting in the spirit of Rubens: swirling movement, rosy flesh, abundant dynamism, dramatic skies, opulent allegory.
artists.negativeHint: sparse minimalism, dry Wyeth austerity
artists.bio: Sir Peter Paul Rubens was a Flemish artist and diplomat. He is considered the most influential artist of the Flemish Baroque tradition. Rubens's highly charged compositions reference erudite aspects of classical and Christian history. His unique and immensely popular Baroque style emphasised movement, colour, and sensuality, which followed the immediate, dramatic artistic style promoted in the Counter-Reformation. Rubens was a painter producing altarpieces, portraits, landscapes, and history paintings of mythological and allegorical subjects. He was also a prolific designer of cartoons for the Flemish tapestry workshops and of frontispieces for the publishers in Antwerp.

artists.name: Diego Velázquez
artists.styleLock: Spanish Baroque painting in the spirit of Velázquez: freestyle brush economy, courtly atmosphere, truthful light, masterpiece spatial ambiguity.
artists.negativeHint: garish Fauvist clash, anime eyes
artists.bio: Diego Velázquez (Baroque ES). Spanish Baroque painting in the spirit of Velázquez: freestyle brush economy, courtly atmosphere, truthful light, masterpiece spatial ambiguity. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: baroque, spain, europe.

artists.name: Francisco Goya
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Goya: psychological darkness or satirical edge, loose late brush, stark contrasts, human folly and dignity.
artists.negativeHint: cute pastel kawaii, clean corporate vector
artists.bio: Francisco José de Goya y Lucientes was a Spanish romantic painter and printmaker. He is considered the most important Spanish artist of the late 18th and early 19th centuries. His paintings, drawings, and engravings reflected contemporary historical upheavals and influenced important 19th- and 20th-century painters. Goya is often referred to as the last of the Old Masters and the first of the moderns. He is widely regarded as one of the most influential figures in the history of Western art.

artists.name: Eugène Delacroix
artists.styleLock: Romantic painting in the spirit of Delacroix: vibrant color, energetic brush, exotic or historical drama, emotional storm.
artists.negativeHint: cool deadpan photography look, neoplastic grid
artists.bio: Eugène Delacroix (Romanticism FR). Romantic painting in the spirit of Delacroix: vibrant color, energetic brush, exotic or historical drama, emotional storm. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: romantic, europe.

artists.name: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres
artists.styleLock: Neoclassical painting in the spirit of Ingres: porcelain finish, sinuous line, idealized form, cool clarity and odalisque elegance.
artists.negativeHint: rough expressionist smear, street graffiti
artists.bio: Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French Neoclassical painter. Ingres was profoundly influenced by past artistic traditions and aspired to become the guardian of academic orthodoxy against the ascendant Romantic style. Although he considered himself a painter of history in the tradition of Nicolas Poussin and Jacques-Louis David, it is his portraits, both painted and drawn, that are recognized as his greatest legacy. His expressive distortions of form and space made him an important precursor of modern art, influencing Henri Matisse, Pablo Picasso, and other modernists.

artists.name: John Constable
artists.styleLock: English landscape painting in the spirit of Constable: lively cloud studies, fresh greens, rural Suffolk light, naturalist sincerity.
artists.negativeHint: desert surrealism, pop Ben-Day dots
artists.bio: John Constable was an English landscape painter in the Romantic tradition. Born in Suffolk, he is known principally for revolutionising the genre of landscape painting with his pictures of Dedham Vale, the area on the borderland of Suffolk and north Essex surrounding his home – now known as "Constable Country" – which he invested with an intensity of affection. "I should paint my own places best", he wrote to his friend John Fisher in 1821, "painting is but another word for feeling."

artists.name: Gustave Courbet
artists.styleLock: Realist painting in the spirit of Courbet: earthy material truth, working figures, dense paint, unidealized rural or studio life.
artists.negativeHint: ethereal Pre-Raphaelite glow, neon night city
artists.bio: Jean Désiré Gustave Courbet was a French painter who led the Realism movement in 19th-century French painting. Committed to painting only what he could see, he rejected academic convention and the Romanticism of the previous generation of visual artists. His independence set an example that was important to later artists, such as the Impressionists and the Cubists. Courbet occupies an important place in 19th-century French painting as an innovator and as an artist willing to make bold social statements through his work.

artists.name: Édouard Manet
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Manet: frank modern subjects, bold flattened blacks, café and park light, bridge between realism and Impressionism.
artists.negativeHint: medieval gold ground icons, pure abstract drip
artists.bio: Édouard Manet (19th c. FR). Painting in the spirit of Manet: frank modern subjects, bold flattened blacks, café and park light, bridge between realism and Impressionism. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: impressionism, modern, europe.

artists.name: Edgar Degas
artists.styleLock: Painting/pastel in the spirit of Degas: asymmetrical crop, dancers and bathers, chalky pastel texture, observational modern life.
artists.negativeHint: centered heraldic symmetry, heavy gothic gloom
artists.bio: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist artist famous for his pastel drawings and oil paintings.

artists.name: Pierre-Auguste Renoir
artists.styleLock: Impressionist painting in the spirit of Renoir: warm dappled light, soft flesh, sociable leisure, feathery brush, rosy atmosphere.
artists.negativeHint: cold industrial Brutalism, harsh tenebrism only
artists.bio: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a leading French Impressionist artist. In his depiction of feminine beauty, Renoir has been described as "the final representative of a tradition which runs directly from Rubens to Watteau."

artists.name: Georges Seurat
artists.styleLock: Pointillist painting in the spirit of Seurat: optical dots of pure color, serene modern parks, scientific calm, luminous stillness.
artists.negativeHint: loose wet-in-wet watercolor chaos, photoreal HDR
artists.bio: Georges Pierre Seurat was a French post-Impressionist artist. He devised the painting techniques known as chromoluminarism and pointillism and used conté crayon for drawings on paper with a rough surface.

artists.name: Paul Gauguin
artists.styleLock: Synthetist painting in the spirit of Gauguin: flat symbolic color, bold outlines, tropical or Breton mythic stillness, decorative primitivist design—avoid colonial caricature; focus on color structure and landscape.
artists.negativeHint: photoreal tourist postcard, grey tonalism
artists.bio: Eugène Henri Paul Gauguin was a French painter, sculptor, printmaker, ceramist, and writer, whose work has been primarily associated with the Post-Impressionist and Symbolist movements. He was also an influential practitioner of wood engraving and woodcuts as art forms. While only moderately successful during his lifetime, Gauguin has since been recognized for his experimental use of color and Synthetist style that were distinct from Impressionism.

artists.name: Henri de Toulouse-Lautrec
artists.styleLock: Belle Époque painting/lithograph spirit: cabaret energy, cropped figures, chalky color, Paris nightlife silhouette without readable posters text.
artists.negativeHint: pastoral Constable greens, minimal white cube
artists.bio: Comte Henri Marie Raymond de Toulouse-Lautrec-Montfa, known as Toulouse-Lautrec, was a French painter, printmaker, draughtsman, caricaturist, and illustrator. His immersion in the colourful and theatrical life of Paris's Belle Époque in the late 19th century allowed him to produce popular works of art from decadent affairs.

artists.name: Edvard Munch
artists.styleLock: Expressionist painting in the spirit of Munch: swirling psychological landscape, anguished color, thin haunted figures, Nordic emotional weather.
artists.negativeHint: cheerful Hockney pools, corporate memphis pattern
artists.bio: Edvard Munch was a Norwegian painter. His 1893 work The Scream has become one of the most iconic and acclaimed images in all of Western art.

artists.name: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner
artists.styleLock: German Expressionist painting: jagged urban figures, acidic color, angular woodcut energy, modern city anxiety.
artists.negativeHint: soft sfumato Renaissance calm, pastel Mucha only
artists.bio: Ernst Ludwig Kirchner was a German expressionist painter and printmaker. He was one of the founders of the artists group Die Brücke or "The Bridge", a key group leading to the foundation of Expressionism in 20th-century art. Kirchner volunteered for army service in the First World War, but soon suffered a breakdown and was discharged. His work was branded as "degenerate" by the Nazis in 1933, and in 1937 more than 600 of his works were sold or destroyed.

artists.name: Wassily Kandinsky
artists.styleLock: Abstract painting in the spirit of Kandinsky: musical color improvisation, floating geometric and organic forms, spiritual synesthesia, no readable symbols.
artists.negativeHint: photoreal street scene, classical portraiture
artists.bio: Wassily Wassilyevich Kandinsky was a Russian painter and art theorist active in Germany during the late Belle Époque and Interwar eras. Kandinsky is generally credited as one of the pioneers of abstraction in Western art. Born in Moscow, he began painting studies at the age of 30.

artists.name: Kazimir Malevich
artists.styleLock: Suprematist abstract painting: floating geometric planes on white infinite space, radical simplicity, cosmic non-objectivity.
artists.negativeHint: busy figurative narrative, impressionist landscape
artists.bio: Kazimir Severinovich Malevich was a Russian avant-garde artist and art theorist, whose work and writings pioneered the development of abstract painting in the 20th century. He is best known as the founder of Suprematism, a radically non-objective form of painting he introduced in 1915.

artists.name: Joan Miró
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Miró: playful biomorphic signs, starry fields, primary accents on soft grounds, childlike cosmic poetry without text.
artists.negativeHint: heavy oil realism, architectural photography
artists.bio: Joan Miró (20th c. ES). Painting in the spirit of Miró: playful biomorphic signs, starry fields, primary accents on soft grounds, childlike cosmic poetry without text. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: surrealism, abstract, europe.

artists.name: Max Ernst
artists.styleLock: Surreal painting in the spirit of Ernst: frottage textures, forest of strange growths, dream archaeology, uncanny natural history.
artists.negativeHint: clean Swiss poster grid, fashion gloss photo
artists.bio: Max Ernst was a German-born painter, sculptor, printmaker, graphic artist, and poet. A prolific artist, Ernst was a pioneer of the Dada movement and surrealism in Europe. He had no formal artistic training, but his experimental attitude toward the making of art resulted in his invention of frottage—a technique that uses pencil rubbings of textured objects and relief surfaces to create images—and grattage, an analogous technique in which paint is scraped across canvas to reveal the imprints of the objects placed beneath. Ernst is noted for his unconventional drawing methods as well as for creating novels and pamphlets using the method of collages. He served as a soldier for four years during...

artists.name: Giorgio de Chirico
artists.styleLock: Metaphysical painting: empty piazzas, long afternoon shadows, classical mannequins, uncanny quiet architecture.
artists.negativeHint: busy impressionist crowd, drip action painting
artists.bio: Giuseppe Maria Alberto Giorgio de Chirico was a Greek-Italian artist and writer born in Volos, Greece. In the years before World War I, he founded the scuola metafisica art movement, which profoundly influenced the surrealists. His best-known works often feature Roman arcades, long shadows, mannequins, trains, and illogical perspective. His imagery reflects his affinity for the philosophy of Arthur Schopenhauer and of Friedrich Nietzsche, and for the mythology of his birthplace.

artists.name: Amedeo Modigliani
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Modigliani: elongated necks and almond eyes, warm earth palette, intimate modernist portrait, mask-like elegance.
artists.negativeHint: cubist shatter, photoreal pores
artists.bio: Amedeo Clemente Modigliani was an Italian painter and sculptor of the École de Paris who worked mainly in France. He is known for portraits and nudes in a modern style characterised by a surreal elongation of faces, necks, and figures — works that were not received well during his lifetime, but later became much sought after. Modigliani was born and spent his youth in Italy, where he studied the art of antiquity and the Renaissance. In 1906, he moved to Paris, where he came into contact with such artists as Pablo Picasso and Constantin Brâncuși. By 1912, Modigliani was exhibiting highly stylised sculptures with Cubists of the Section d'Or group at the Salon d'Automne.

artists.name: Egon Schiele
artists.styleLock: Expressionist drawing/painting in the spirit of Schiele: contorted line, raw psychological figure, stark contour, urgent flesh tones.
artists.negativeHint: smooth Ingres porcelain, cheerful Renoir picnic
artists.bio: Egon Leo Adolf Ludwig Schiele was an Austrian Expressionist painter. His work is noted for its intensity and its raw sexuality, and for the many self-portraits the artist produced, including nude self-portraits. The twisted body shapes and the expressive line that characterise Schiele's paintings and drawings mark the artist as an early exponent of Expressionism. Gustav Klimt, a figurative painter of the early 20th century, was a mentor to Schiele.

artists.name: Francis Bacon
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Francis Bacon: visceral figure distortion in geometric cages, smeared flesh, existential drama, controlled chaos.
artists.negativeHint: cute illustration, calm Vermeer interior
artists.bio: Francis Bacon, 1st Viscount St Alban was an English philosopher and statesman who served as Attorney General and Lord Chancellor of England under King James I. Bacon argued for the importance of natural philosophy, guided by the scientific method, and his works remained influential throughout the Scientific Revolution.

artists.name: Lucian Freud
artists.styleLock: Painted flesh realism in the spirit of Lucian Freud: thick impasto skin, unflinching portrait, studio glare, psychological weight.
artists.negativeHint: airbrushed beauty ads, abstract color field only
artists.bio: Lucian Michael Freud was a British painter and draughtsman, specialising in figurative art, who is known as one of the foremost 20th-century English portraitists.

artists.name: Gerhard Richter
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Gerhard Richter: photo-blur oil squeegee, or abstract scraped color veils, cool German contemporary ambiguity.
artists.negativeHint: ukiyo-e flat prints, neon pop comics
artists.bio: Gerhard Richter is a German visual artist. Richter has produced abstract as well as photorealistic paintings, photographs and glass pieces. He is widely regarded as one of the most important contemporary German artists and several of his works have set record prices at auction, with him being the most expensive living painter at one time.

artists.name: Peter Doig
artists.styleLock: Contemporary painting in the spirit of Peter Doig: dreamlike landscape memory, cinematic color, soft mystery, filmic stillness.
artists.negativeHint: hard Bauhaus geometry, reportage flash photo
artists.bio: Peter Doig is a British painter who has lived and worked between England, Scotland, Trinidad, Canada, the USA and Germany. He settled in Trinidad with his family between 2002 and 2021, when he moved back to London.

artists.name: Luc Tuymans
artists.styleLock: Contemporary painting in the spirit of Tuymans: washed pale memory images, quiet political afterimage, thin paint, muted unease.
artists.negativeHint: high-chroma Fauvism, glossy fashion photo
artists.bio: Luc Tuymans is a Belgian visual artist best known for his paintings which explore people's relationship with history and confront their ability to ignore it. World War II is a recurring theme in his work. He is a key figure of the generation of European figurative painters who gained renown at a time when many believed the medium had lost its relevance due to the new digital age.

artists.name: Chris Ofili-adjacent decorative figuration
artists.styleLock: Contemporary decorative figuration: luminous layered pattern, rich color, mythical modern figures, ornate surface without cultural caricature.
artists.negativeHint: stark Brutalist grey photo, minimal Mondrian only
artists.bio: Christopher Ofili is a British painter who won the Turner Prize in 1998. He has used resin, beads, oil paint, glitter, lumps of elephant dung and cut-outs from pornographic magazines as painting elements. Ofili's work has been classified as punk art. He currently lives in Trinidad.

artists.name: El Anatsui-adjacent shimmering assemblage
artists.styleLock: Shimmering metallic tapestry-like surface energy inspired by El Anatsui: cascading bottle-cap glints as abstract landscape of light, African contemporary monumental shimmer—painterly, not literal sculpture photo.
artists.negativeHint: smooth Renaissance sfumato portraits
artists.bio: El Anatsui is a Ghanaian sculptor active for much of his career in Nigeria. He has drawn particular international attention for his "bottle-top installations". These installations consist of thousands of aluminum pieces sourced from alcohol recycling stations and sewn together with copper wire, which are then transformed into metallic cloth-like wall sculptures. Such materials, while seemingly stiff and sturdy, are actually free and flexible, which often helps with manipulation when installing his sculptures.

artists.name: William Kentridge
artists.styleLock: Charcoal animation-still spirit of Kentridge: sooty erasures, processional figures, Johannesburg industrial melancholy, drawn cinema.
artists.negativeHint: candy pop Ben-Day, clean vector logos
artists.bio: William Kentridge is a South African artist best known for his prints, drawings, and animated films. He is especially noted for a sequence of hand-drawn animated films he produced during the 1990s, constructed by filming a drawing, making erasures and changes, and filming it again. He continues this process meticulously, giving each change to the drawing a quarter of a second's to two seconds' screen time. A single drawing will be altered and filmed this way until the end of a scene. These palimpsest-like drawings are later displayed along with the films as finished pieces of art.

artists.name: Ouattara Watts-adjacent afro-modern
artists.styleLock: Afro-modern abstract painting: symbolic signs, rich earth and cosmic blues, layered cultural glyphs without readable text, spiritual energy.
artists.negativeHint: Dutch Golden Age still-life only
artists.bio: Ouattara Watts is an Ivory Coast-born American visual artist, known for his multimedia paintings that incorporate African and Western aesthetics and depict themes of spirituality and modernity. His work has been exhibited in reputable collections internationally, and he is classified by Christie's as a "Top Artist."

artists.name: Alma Thomas
artists.styleLock: Abstract painting in the spirit of Alma Thomas: mosaic dashes of bright color, radiant garden-like fields, joyful rhythmic pattern.
artists.negativeHint: tenebrist Caravaggio drama, grey documentary photo
artists.bio: Alma Woodsey Thomas was an American artist and art teacher who lived and worked in Washington, D.C., and is now recognized as a major American painter of the 20th century. She is the first African-American woman to be included in the White House's permanent art collection. Thomas is best known for the "exuberant", colorful, abstract paintings that she created after she retired from a 35-year career teaching art at Washington's Shaw Junior High School.

artists.name: Norman Lewis
artists.styleLock: Abstract painting in the spirit of Norman Lewis: calligraphic night processions, sparks of color in dark fields, lyrical social abstraction.
artists.negativeHint: hard Mondrian grid only, tourist postcard
artists.bio: Norman Lewis (20th c. US). Abstract painting in the spirit of Norman Lewis: calligraphic night processions, sparks of color in dark fields, lyrical social abstraction. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: abstract, north-america.

artists.name: Jacob Lawrence
artists.styleLock: Modernist narrative painting in the spirit of Jacob Lawrence: flat tempera planes, strong design, Migration-series clarity, dignified storytelling without text.
artists.negativeHint: soft Impressionist haze, photoreal HDR
artists.bio: Jacob Armstead Lawrence was an American painter known for his portrayal of African-American historical subjects and contemporary life. Lawrence referred to his style as "dynamic cubism", an art form popularized in Europe which drew great inspiration from West African and Meso-American art. For his compositions, Lawrence found inspiration in everyday life in Harlem. He brought the African-American experience to life using blacks and browns juxtaposed with vivid colors. Lawrence also taught and spent 16 years as a professor at the University of Washington.

artists.name: Romare Bearden
artists.styleLock: Collage painting in the spirit of Bearden: jazz-era cut paper figures, rich pattern, Harlem memory, layered photographic fragments as design.
artists.negativeHint: empty color-field rectangles only
artists.bio: Romare Howard Bearden was an American artist, author, and songwriter. He worked with many types of media including cartoons, oils, and collages. Born in Charlotte, North Carolina, Bearden grew up in New York City and Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and graduated from New York University in 1935.

artists.name: Alice Neel
artists.styleLock: Portrait painting in the spirit of Alice Neel: psychologically direct sitters, candid contour, unvarnished modern life, intimate studio honesty.
artists.negativeHint: glamour retouch photo, abstract drip only
artists.bio: Alice Neel was an American visual artist. Recognized for her paintings of friends, family, lovers, poets, artists, and strangers, Neel is considered one of the greatest American portraitists of the 20th century. Her career spanned from the 1920s to 1980s.

artists.name: Diego Rivera
artists.styleLock: Mexican muralism in the spirit of Rivera: monumental workers and history, solid volumes, public narrative fresco energy, earth and sky clarity—no slogans.
artists.negativeHint: tiny intimate Dutch interior only, soft Whistler nocturne
artists.bio: Diego María de la Concepción Juan Nepomuceno Estanislao de la Rivera y Barrientos Acosta y Rodríguez was a Mexican painter. His large frescoes helped establish the mural movement in Mexican and international art.

artists.name: José Clemente Orozco
artists.styleLock: Mexican muralism in the spirit of Orozco: tragic monumental figures, fiery allegory, stark architectural drama, moral force.
artists.negativeHint: pastel Impressionist picnic, cute stickers
artists.bio: José Clemente Orozco (20th c. MX). Mexican muralism in the spirit of Orozco: tragic monumental figures, fiery allegory, stark architectural drama, moral force. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: muralism, latin-america.

artists.name: David Alfaro Siqueiros
artists.styleLock: Mexican muralism in the spirit of Siqueiros: dynamic foreshortening, industrial modernity, bold polyangular composition, revolutionary energy without text.
artists.negativeHint: quiet Vermeer room, sumi empty mist only
artists.bio: David Alfaro Siqueiros was a Mexican social realist painter, best known for his large public murals using the latest in equipment, materials and technique. Along with Diego Rivera and José Clemente Orozco, he was one of the most famous of the "Mexican muralists".

artists.name: Rufino Tamayo
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Tamayo: saturated Mexican color, simplified mythic figures, textured modern surfaces, lyrical primitivism.
artists.negativeHint: grey Richter blur photo, Swiss grid poster
artists.bio: Rufino del Carmen Arellanes Tamayo was a Mexican painter of Zapotec heritage, born in Oaxaca de Juárez, Mexico. Tamayo was active in the mid-20th century in Mexico and New York, painting figurative abstraction with surrealist influences.

artists.name: Fernando Botero
artists.styleLock: Figurative painting in the spirit of Botero: volumetric inflated forms, satirical plump dignity, smooth Colombian color, monumental stillness.
artists.negativeHint: elongated Schiele line, drip Pollock chaos
artists.bio: Fernando Botero Angulo was a Colombian painter and sculptor. His signature style, also known as "Boterismo", depicts people and figures in large, exaggerated volume, which can represent political criticism or humor, depending on the piece. He was considered the most recognized and quoted artist from Latin America in his lifetime, and his art can be found in highly visible places around the world, such as Park Avenue in New York City and the Champs-Élysées in Paris, at different times.

artists.name: Wifredo Lam
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Wifredo Lam: Afro-Cuban surreal hybrid figures, jungle verticals, spiritual modernism, masked metamorphosis.
artists.negativeHint: English Constable pasture, clean Bauhaus bars
artists.bio: Wifredo Óscar de la Concepción Lam y Castilla, better known as Wifredo Lam, was a Cuban artist who sought to portray and revive the enduring Afro-Cuban spirit and culture. Inspired by and in contact with some of the most renowned artists of the 20th century, including Pablo Picasso, Henri Matisse, Frida Kahlo, and Diego Rivera, Lam melded his influences and created a unique style, which was ultimately characterized by the prominence of hybrid figures. This distinctive visual style of his also influenced many artists. Though he was predominantly a painter, he also worked with sculpture, ceramics, and printmaking in his later life.

artists.name: Roberto Matta
artists.styleLock: Surreal biomorphic space in the spirit of Matta: psychic morphologies, cosmic architecture, electric Latin American surrealism.
artists.negativeHint: Dutch still-life breakfast, photoreal food
artists.bio: Roberto Antonio Sebástian Matta-Echaurren, usually known simply as Matta, also as  Sebastián Matta or Roberto Matta, was one of Chile's best-known painters and figures in 20th century surrealist art across the Americas and Europe.

artists.name: Tarsila do Amaral
artists.styleLock: Brazilian modernism in the spirit of Tarsila: anthropophagic landscape, bold simplified forms, tropical color, Antropofagia clarity.
artists.negativeHint: foggy Whistler nocturne, grey concrete only
artists.bio: Tarsila de Aguiar do Amaral was a Brazilian painter, draftswoman, and translator. She is considered one of the leading Latin American modernist artists, and is regarded as the painter who best achieved Brazilian aspirations for nationalistic expression in a modern style. As a member of the Grupo dos Cinco, Tarsila is also considered a major influence in the modern art movement in Brazil, alongside Anita Malfatti, Menotti Del Picchia, Mário de Andrade, and Oswald de Andrade. She was instrumental in the formation of the aesthetic movement, Antropofagia (1928–1929); in fact, Tarsila was the one with her celebrated painting, Abaporu, who inspired Oswald de Andrade's famous Manifesto Antropófago.

artists.name: Cândido Portinari
artists.styleLock: Brazilian modernist painting in the spirit of Portinari: social dignity of workers, earth pigments, mural-scale humanity, coffee and drought narratives without text.
artists.negativeHint: pop Ben-Day irony, neon night Tokyo
artists.bio: Cândido Portinari (20th c. BR). Brazilian modernist painting in the spirit of Portinari: social dignity of workers, earth pigments, mural-scale humanity, coffee and drought narratives without text. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: modernism, latin-america.

artists.name: Yayoi Kusama
artists.styleLock: Painting/installation spirit of Kusama: infinity nets and polka dots, obsessive pattern, pumpkin-bright color fields, mirrored infinity sensation as 2D pattern world.
artists.negativeHint: Caravaggio tenebrism, sober court portrait
artists.bio: Yayoi Kusama  was a Japanese contemporary artist who worked primarily in sculpture and installation. She was also active in painting, performance, video art, fashion, poetry, fiction, and other arts. Her work was based in conceptual art and shows some attributes of feminism, minimalism, surrealism, art brut, pop art, and abstract expressionism, and is infused with autobiographical, psychological, and sexual content. She was acknowledged as one of the most important artists to have come out of Japan, and was one of the world's top-selling female artists and ranked #19 in Sotheby's 2023 list of the top 50 artists. Her work influenced her contemporaries, including Andy Warhol and Claes Oldenbur...

artists.name: Takashi Murakami-adjacent superflat
artists.styleLock: Superflat graphic painting: high-chroma cute-fierce motifs, flat commercial sheen, anime-adjacent pop without logos or readable text.
artists.negativeHint: Rembrandt brown umbers, documentary grit photo
artists.bio: Takashi Murakami  is a Japanese contemporary artist. He works in fine arts as well as commercial media and is known for blurring the line between high and low arts. His work draws from the aesthetic characteristics of the Japanese artistic tradition and the nature of postwar Japanese culture. He has designed covers for several hip hop albums, namely Kanye West's Graduation (2007), Future's eponymous fifth studio album (2017), West and Kid Cudi's Kids See Ghosts (2018), and Juice Wrld's posthumous The Party Never Ends (2024).

artists.name: Yoshitomo Nara
artists.styleLock: Painting in the spirit of Nara: large-headed figures, sparse ground, quiet rebellious cuteness, flat pastel contemporary Japanese pop.
artists.negativeHint: busy Baroque allegory, Gursky mega-crowd
artists.bio: Yoshitomo Nara  is a Japanese artist. He lives and works in Nasushiobara, Tochigi Prefecture, though his artwork has been exhibited worldwide. Nara has had nearly 40 solo exhibitions since 1984. His art work has been housed at the MoMA and the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA). His most well-known and repeated subjects are "big-headed girls" with piercing eyes, who one Nara scholar describes as having "childlike expressions [that] resonate with adult emotions, [their] embodiment of kawaii (cuteness) carries a dark humor, and any explicit cultural references are intertwined with personal memories."

artists.name: Chinese contemporary conceptual graphic
artists.styleLock: Contemporary Chinese conceptual graphic: stark monumental simplicity, political poetry as pure form, black-red-wood material clarity—no slogans or portraits of living leaders.
artists.negativeHint: rococo ornament overload, soft Renoir flesh
artists.bio: Chinese contemporary conceptual graphic (contemporary CN). Contemporary Chinese conceptual graphic: stark monumental simplicity, political poetry as pure form, black-red-wood material clarity—no slogans or portraits of living leaders. Graphic / print visual language. Associated tags: contemporary, asia, china.

artists.name: Chinese literati landscape
artists.styleLock: Chinese literati ink landscape: towering mist mountains, empty-far composition, calligraphic texture strokes, poetic scholar solitude on silk/paper.
artists.negativeHint: Western oil impasto, neon cyberpunk
artists.bio: Chinese literati landscape (classical CN). Chinese literati ink landscape: towering mist mountains, empty-far composition, calligraphic texture strokes, poetic scholar solitude on silk/paper. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: ink, landscape, asia, china.

artists.name: Qi Baishi
artists.styleLock: Chinese ink-and-color painting in the spirit of Qi Baishi: lively shrimp, frogs, blossoms; playful brush economy, folk warmth, expressive simplicity.
artists.negativeHint: photoreal macro dew, Constructivist diagonals
artists.bio: Qi Baishi was a Chinese painter, noted for the whimsical, often playful style of his works. Born to a peasant family from Xiangtan, Hunan, Qi taught himself to paint, sparked by the Manual of the Mustard Seed Garden. After he turned 40, he traveled, visiting various scenic spots in China. After 1917 he settled in Beijing. Qi was the master of Hu Jieqing, the wife of Lao She.

artists.name: Xu Beihong
artists.styleLock: Modern Chinese ink painting in the spirit of Xu Beihong: powerful horses or figures, Western anatomy meeting ink brush, heroic vitality.
artists.negativeHint: kawaii superflat stickers, soft Monet waterlilies only
artists.bio: Xu Beihong (20th c. CN). Modern Chinese ink painting in the spirit of Xu Beihong: powerful horses or figures, Western anatomy meeting ink brush, heroic vitality. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: ink, asia, china.

artists.name: Bada Shanren
artists.styleLock: Chinese ink painting in the spirit of Bada Shanren: lonely birds and rocks, eccentric abbreviated brush, ironic emptiness, literati solitude.
artists.negativeHint: busy Venetian colorito, fashion editorial gloss
artists.bio: Bada Shanren (Qing CN). Chinese ink painting in the spirit of Bada Shanren: lonely birds and rocks, eccentric abbreviated brush, ironic emptiness, literati solitude. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: ink, asia, china.

artists.name: Utagawa Hiroshige
artists.styleLock: Ukiyo-e landscape in the spirit of Hiroshige: poetic rain and bridges, travel views, atmospheric Japanese weather, woodblock color bands.
artists.negativeHint: Cubist facets, heavy oil portraiture
artists.bio: Utagawa Hiroshige  or Andō Hiroshige , born Andō Tokutarō, was a Japanese ukiyo-e artist, considered the last great master of that tradition.

artists.name: Kitagawa Utamaro
artists.styleLock: Ukiyo-e bijin-ga spirit of Utamaro: elegant feminine contour, patterned kimono, refined close-up composition, soft mineral color—graceful, not exploitative.
artists.negativeHint: sports action freeze-frame, Brutalist concrete
artists.bio: Kitagawa Utamaro  was a Japanese artist. He is one of the most highly regarded designers of ukiyo-e woodblock prints and paintings, and is best known for his bijin ōkubi-e "large-headed pictures of beautiful women" of the 1790s. He also produced nature studies, particularly illustrated books of insects.

artists.name: Sesshū Tōyō
artists.styleLock: Japanese ink landscape in the spirit of Sesshū: bold haboku splashed ink, monumental cliffs, Zen austerity, powerful empty space.
artists.negativeHint: candy-colored pop art, photoreal food
artists.bio: Sesshū Tōyō (Muromachi JP). Japanese ink landscape in the spirit of Sesshū: bold haboku splashed ink, monumental cliffs, Zen austerity, powerful empty space. Painterly fine-art visual language. Associated tags: ink, asia, japan.

artists.name: Raja Ravi Varma
artists.styleLock: Indo-academic oil painting in the spirit of Raja Ravi Varma: mythic narrative clarity, luminous saris, theatrical Indian storytelling light.
artists.negativeHint: sumi mist monochrome only, Swiss red-black poster
artists.bio: Raja Ravi Varma was an Indian painter. His works are one of the best examples of the fusion of European academic art with a purely Indian sensibility and iconography. He greatly enhanced his reach and influence as a painter and public figure by making affordable lithographs of his paintings available to the public. His lithographs increased the involvement of common people with fine arts and defined artistic tastes. Furthermore, his religious depictions of Hindu deities and works from Indian epic poetry and Puranas have received critical acclaim. He was part of the royal family of Parappanad, Malappuram district.

artists.name: Abanindranath Tagore
artists.styleLock: Bengal School wash painting: misty tempera-like washes, lyrical Indian revival, soft contours, poetic nationalism as atmosphere not slogan.
artists.negativeHint: hard pop Ben-Day, Gursky stadium crowds
artists.bio: Abanindranath Tagore was an Indian painter who was the principal artist and creator of the Indian Society of Oriental Art in 1907. He was also the first major exponent of Swadeshi values in Indian art. He founded the influential Bengal school of art, which led to the development of modern Indian painting. He was also a noted writer, particularly for children. Popularly known as 'Aban Thakur', his books Rajkahini, Buro Angla, Nalak, and Khirer Putul were landmarks in Bengali language children's literature and art.

artists.name: Amrita Sher-Gil
artists.styleLock: Modernist painting in the spirit of Amrita Sher-Gil: solid figures, earthy Indian palette, melancholic dignity, Post-Impressionist structure.
artists.negativeHint: ukiyo-e tourist Mount Fuji cliché, neon Tokyo nights
artists.bio: Amrita Sher-Gil was a Hungarian–Indian painter. She has been called "one of the greatest avant-garde women artists of the early 20th century" and a pioneer in modern Indian art. Drawn to painting from an early age, Sher-Gil started formal lessons at the age of eight. She first gained recognition at the age of 19, for her 1932 oil painting Young Girls. artists.bio: Andy Warhol was an American artist and filmmaker. Widely regarded as the most important artist of the second half of the 20th century, Warhol's practice spanned various media, including painting, filmmaking, photography, publishing, and performance art. A leading figure in the Pop art movement, his work explores the relationship between advertising, consumerism, mass media, and celebrity culture. His embrace of mechanical reproduction challenged traditional boundaries between high and low culture. He is also credited with popularizing the expression "15 minutes of fame."

Lichtenstein's art is represented in major museum collections worldwide, and he remains one of the most influential and recognizable artists of the 20th century.

Born in 1888 in Bottrop, Westphalia, Germany, into a Roman Catholic family with a background in craftsmanship, Albers received practical training in diverse skills like engraving glass, plumbing, and wiring during his childhood. He later worked as a schoolteacher from 1908 to 1913 and received his first public commission in 1918 and moved to Munich in 1919.

Beardsley's contribution to the development of the Art Nouveau and poster styles was significant despite his early death from tuberculosis. He is one of the important Modern Style figures.

artists.bio: Edmund Dulac was a French-British naturalised magazine illustrator, book illustrator and stamp designer. Born in Toulouse, he studied law but later turned to the study of art at the École des Beaux-Arts. He moved to London early in the 20th century and in 1905 received his first commission to illustrate the novels of the Brontë Sisters. During World War I, Dulac produced relief books. After the war, the deluxe children's book market shrank, and he then turned to magazine illustrations among other ventures. He designed banknotes during World War II and postage stamps, most notably those that heralded the beginning of Queen Elizabeth II's reign.

He achieved acclaim with Where the Wild Things Are (1963), the first of a trilogy followed by In the Night Kitchen (1970) and Outside Over There (1981). He also designed sets for operas, notably Mozart's The Magic Flute.

She was awarded a National Medal of Arts from the National Endowment for the Arts in 1998. She was elected to the Royal Canadian Academy of Arts in 2004.

She belonged to a group called "The Five", a circle of women inspired by Theosophy who shared a belief in the importance of trying to contact the "High Masters", often through séances. Her paintings, which sometimes resemble diagrams, were a visual representation of complex spiritual ideas.

artists.bio: Anita Catarina Malfatti was a Brazilian artist. She is heralded as the first one to introduce European and American forms of Modernism to Brazil. Her solo exhibition in São Paulo, in 1917–1918, was controversial at the time, and her expressionist style and subjects were revolutionary for the complacently old-fashioned art expectations of Brazilians who were searching for a national identity in art, but who were not prepared for the influences Malfatti would bring to the country. Malfatti's presence was also highly felt during the Week of Modern Art in 1922, where she and the Group of Five made huge revolutionary changes in the structure and response to modern art in Brazil.

Koesoema, who was a surveyor at a local sugar factory, Affandi finished his upper secondary school in Jakarta. He gave up his studies to pursue his desire to become an artist. Beginning in 1934, Affandi began teaching himself how to paint. He married Maryati, a fellow artist. One of his children, Kartika, also became an artist. Affandi is considered Indonesia's foremost Expressionist painter.

He joined the Royal Photographic Society in 1937 and gained his Associateship in 1940 and Fellowship in 1942. and in 1980, the Photographic Society of America named him one of the world's top ten master photographers. He was the first Chinese photographer to take artistic nude shots, and was also known for the unique "composite photography" technique he created.

In 1922 she moved to Mexico, where she became an active member of the Mexican Communist Party.
